title: Khazars
fact_summary: A steppe power north of the Caucasus. The Byzantine chapter on the Hungarians says the two peoples once lived and fought together.

claims.text: Chapter 38 of De Administrando Imperio says the “Turks” (the Hungarians) once settled near Khazaria, lived with the Khazars “for three years” and fought alongside them in all their wars.
claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth reports it.

claims.text: The same chapter tells of the Khazar marriage of Levedi, a Hungarian leader, and of his visit to Khazaria.
claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth reports it.

claims.text: The alliance between the Hungarians and the Khazars was short, and can be dated either to 859–861 or to about 870–880.
claims.certainty_reason: Rests on reading the chapter's “three years” as written, which many scholars do not accept.

claims.text: The “three years” is a copying error for a much longer time, such as 200 or 300 years.

held_by.who: Most earlier researchers, as reported by Tóth (2015). Their works have not been opened yet.

claims.certainty_reason: Known here only through a study that argues against it.

contradictions.what_differs: How long the Hungarians lived with the Khazars: three years, as the oldest copy has it, or centuries.

open_questions.text: Do any Khazar or Arabic sources mention the Hungarians?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
